newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Vanclief reviews ag cost-recover programs.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Vanclief reviews ag cost-recover programs.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Lyle Vanclief said his department is reviewing the repercussions of its cost-recovery programs on Canadian farmers, the Canadian Press reported.
"We can find more ways of cost avoidance and cost reduction because nobody likes cost recovery," Vanclief said in an interview Thursday with the Canadian Press.
Agriculture Canada's cost-recovery program is part of the federal government's budget restraint program. It seeks to recover the cost of most services offered to the agriculture industry.
The program has been criticized for its sharp increase in inspection fees, in some cases as much as 900 percent in the last five years.
"What we are doing is we are assessing the repercussions of cost-recovery fees that have been put in place. We are in the process of doing that," Vanclief told Canadian Press.
